newsitem.title: UK: EURO OIL SWAPS UP LED BY MOGAS, GAS OIL, JET LOWER.
newsitem.headline: EURO OIL SWAPS UP LED BY MOGAS, GAS OIL, JET LOWER.

text.p: European oil swaps were seen firmer on Wednesday on most products led by gasoline, but gas oil and jet differentials were seen edging lower on expectations of greater availability over coming months.

Brent CFDs experienced a very quiet, deal-dry day with Aug 13-15 offers slightly higher at -27 cents but bids steady at -30 cents. The Aug 18-22 week was meanwhile seen three cents down at -28 to -23 cents, with following weeks also seen weaker.
While gas oil cracks against Brent were seen as steady as they have been all week, jet and EN590 swap deals were heard done around $0.25-$0.50 lower than values seen a day earlier.

Jet deals were reported by brokers at $18.75 premium for September, $24.50 for the fourth quarter and $25.75 for first quarter 1998, while at least one EN590 deal was rumoured done at $8.50 for fourth quarter.
That level was later seen offered as September EN590 was heard offered at $6.00, $0.50 lower on the day as fourth quarter 0.2 diesel was talked a touch lower at $2.25-$2.75.
Heavy fuel oil trades at $95.75 and $95.50 for September indicated a $1.50 rise in levels as the low sulphur market remained quiet and the HSFO/LSFO differential was seen unchanged at around $2.00.

Gasoline swaps jumped $7.50 on August and around $4 on September on fresh U.S. stock drawdown figures, much higher NYMEX unleaded gasoline levels and a still fairly tight prompt barge market, dealers said.

Deals were heard at $218 for August and $200.50 for September later in the day, leaving September crack offers a massive $0.60 higher at $5.2, although fourth quarter and beyond cracks were seen broadly unchanged.
